title: The entire AI layer is untested — 8 modules, and the ones carrying the most findings
detail: summarize, quiz, chat, tts, recommend, client, schemas and prompts have no colocated tests. Only errors.ts and apiKey.ts do. Every unvalidated-model-JSON defect (S032, S062, F005, F030, F034, F035) lives in exactly the files with no test to catch a regression. 44 of 65 source files have no colocated test; the AI layer is the part where that matters most.

title: The declared Node engine is one the dependencies disclaim
detail: engines.node says >=20.19, jsdom@30 requires ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26, and CI pins 22. A contributor who trusts package.json and installs on Node 20.19 gets an EBADENGINE warning and an unsupported test environment. The CI file even carries a comment explaining the real constraint — it just never made it into engines.

title: The backup format silently omits the profile and every review card
detail: LibraryExport carries books and summaries only. Moving to a new device therefore loses the reading goal, bio, chosen voice, theme, and the entire spaced-repetition schedule — the one dataset in the app that cannot be regenerated, because rebuilding it means paying for every quiz again. Nothing in the export UI says so.

title: The repo modules disagree with each other about cascading and about what they accept
detail: books.remove and profiles.remove cascade; summaries.remove does not. create takes a partial input object, update takes a whole entity, upsert takes a whole entity — three conventions across five modules. listByProfile uses an index, listByBook full-scans. A caller cannot predict any of it from the shape.

title: Migration-before-read is a load-bearing ordering enforced only by statement order in one effect
detail: migrateLegacyData() must complete before profileRepo.list() or a legacy user sees an empty profile picker and can create a duplicate. Nothing encodes that dependency — no guard, no marker check at the repo layer, just two awaits in sequence inside a component. Any future caller that reads profiles earlier reintroduces the bug.

title: No deploy workflow exists despite the README pointing at a hosted demo
detail: Only ci.yml is present. The Pages deployment the plan and README describe was never written, so the 'live demo' link the project is meant to lead with has nothing behind it. CI also has no concurrency group, so rapid pushes queue redundant full runs.

title: Raw SDK errors are console-logged without scrubbing — PLAUSIBLE key exposure, needs verification
detail: Five call sites do console.error('...', err) with the untouched SDK error. Google client libraries sometimes embed the full request URL in error detail, and the Gemini REST endpoint carries the key as ?key=. If that holds for @google/genai 2.x, the user's key is printed to the console on every failure. I have not confirmed the SDK's error shape, so this is flagged rather than asserted.

title: Pinning strategy is inconsistent and nothing checks for advisories
detail: react-router, eslint, prettier, globals, typescript-eslint and @eslint/js are pinned exactly while everything else floats on a caret, with no comment explaining the split. CI runs no npm audit and there is no Dependabot config, so a published advisory in any of 288 packages surfaces to nobody.

title: CLAUDE.md documents a NightyTidy run date and nothing about the project
detail: The file a future agent loads first says only 'NightyTidy — Last Run: 2026-05-07'. None of the invariants this codebase actually depends on are written down anywhere it will be read: no key in the bundle, no binary data in book records, lib/ stays framework-free, ArrayBuffer not Blob in IndexedDB, threads pool on Windows. Each of those was learned the hard way and each is one careless edit from being undone.

title: Suite wall-clock is dominated by environment construction, not by tests
detail: 176 tests take 126s, of which the reported environment time is 430s of worker time across the pool. jsdom plus fake-indexeddb plus jest-dom is rebuilt for all 24 files including the twelve that touch no DOM at all. Splitting node-environment tests from jsdom ones via environmentMatchGlobs would cut the common case substantially.

title: Errors reaching the boundary are not recorded anywhere the user can retrieve
detail: For a local-first app with no server this is largely correct, but a user reporting a bug has nothing to send: no error detail surfaced in the UI, no copyable diagnostic, nine scattered console calls and no consistent prefix to grep for.

title: The single highest-value missing feature is a Summarise button
detail: Goodreads import is the headline acquisition feature and it deliberately creates unsummarised books, but there is no action anywhere that turns one into a summarised book. Every other AI capability is gated behind having a summary, so the import funnel terminates in a dead end. This is one button wired to summarizeBook plus saveSummary, and it unlocks chat, quiz, audio, deep dive and the review deck for every imported title.

title: NEGATIVE RESULT — no scar tissue found
detail: Zero TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error or eslint-disable comments across 65 source files. .env.example is accurate and explains why no build-time key exists. Reported so the absence is on record rather than assumed unchecked.

title: NEGATIVE RESULT — layering is proportionate
detail: Three contexts (Profile, Library, Shell), a repo module, and a lib/ that genuinely stays framework-free. No premature plugin systems, no abstractions with a single implementation, no layers that exist for one consumer. The oversized files are a decomposition problem, not an architecture problem.

title: No import path is safe to retry after a partial failure
detail: Both importLibrary and importGoodreadsRows write row by row with no transaction and no resume marker. A failure at book 200 of 300 leaves 199 written; the user's only recourse is to run it again, which re-walks the whole file and — for the JSON path — rewrites every summary (S001).

title: Two error messages point at a Settings screen that does not exist
detail: invalid-key says 'Check it in Settings and try again' and there is no settings surface for the key — ApiKeyDialog is only reachable when the shell decides to open it, which four of six AI call sites never do (S092).

title: README forward-references packaging that does not exist yet
detail: It points readers at a hosted demo, screenshots and a contributing guide, and at docs/superpowers/ for design. The docs directory is real; LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, the demo and the screenshots are not. Honest about being pre-Phase-4, but the links are dead today.
